articles.title_orig: Russia says plague institute worker's death does not risk an epidemic
articles.title_zh: Russia says plague institute worker's death does not risk an epidemic
articles.content_orig:
The victim was working at the anti-plague institute in the Siberia city of Irkutsk
US President Donald Trump has said he will speak with Vladimir Putin soon about the death of a lab worker at a plague research centre in Siberia.
"So far we are in very deep discussions," Trump said, adding that he would be able to report on his talks with the Russian leader "probably" on Thursday. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said no phone call had been scheduled.
Russian officials say they are investigating the cause of the 28-year-old's death and have not confirmed that the suspected disease is pneumonic plague. They insist there is no risk of an epidemic.
Mongolia has ordered "surveillance measures" on its border, AFP reports, while Lithuania has made preparations for any possible case.
Pneumonic plague is a serious lung infection, often described as the most virulent form of plague.
The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) has called for transparency from Russia.
"Timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks," Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said.
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Putin's spokesman said Russia's reporting of the death to the WHO was in line with standard practice, and accused the media of reporting "false information".
The US has issued a formal diplomatic message to Russia requesting additional information. Peskov told reporters he was not aware of such a request.
Reports first emerged on Friday of almost 200 people being placed under observation in Siberia's Irkutsk region following the death.
The lab worker, named in Russian media as Darya Shipilova, had reportedly fallen ill a couple of days earlier.
Unconfirmed reports suggested that she had become ill after either breaking a test tube containing the pathogen at the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East where she worked or following a field trip to a region where plague occurs naturally among wild rodents.
As the US and the WHO sought more information, the country's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, issued a statement saying "there are no epidemic risks for the population of Irkutsk and the Irkutsk region".
It said more than 90% of the people who had been in contact with the victim had "completed medical observation" and "no health disorders associated with infectious pathology were detected".
Neighbouring Mongolia's government has ordered "health surveillance" measures on its border with Russia, AFP news agency reported. The country's health ministry said it would "maintain continuous surveillance and monitoring to prevent potential risks".
This was a precautionary measure, it said, adding "the current risk level is low."
Lithuania's health ministry said it has made preparations to manage any possible case in the country.
Laboratory testing is available, patients would be isolated in infectious disease hospitals, contacts would be identified, and the country has the stocks of medicines suitable for treatment, according to Nerija Kaulakien, an adviser at the Ministry of Health's Communications Division, in an interview with ELTA news agency.
There was no evidence of "an increased risk of plague" at the moment, she said.
In the immediate wake of the laboratory worker's death, Russia's health watchdog had issued a statement saying the woman had died of "pneumonia of an undetermined etiology" and that testing found "no microorganisms related to her professional activities".
However, after this announcement, a pro-government federal news outlet deleted five posts mentioning a possible plague case, and authorities in the town of Baikalsk deleted a message advising against travel to Shelekhov because of a possible plague infection.
Ongoing speculation into the lab worker's death has sparked a back and forth between Russia and the US, with questions about a possible spread outside of Russia.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the US had "measures" available to help Russia if the situation turned out to be more serious than claimed.
According to the WHO, pneumonic plague has a very short incubation period - sometimes just 24 hours - and can be fatal, if not diagnosed and treated early.
People can be infected through:
contact with bodily fluids or contaminated materials
the inhalation of respiratory particles
Symptoms include shortness of breath and coughing, often with blood-tainted phlegm.
The bacterium that causes the plague, Yersinia pestis, found among rodents such as marmots in the area.
It killed up to half the population of Europe in the 14th Century when it was known as the Black Death .
It was in response to an outbreak in the 1920s that the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East, was founded just over 100 years ago.

articles.title_orig: China’s thorium-229 nuclear clock beats Vienna’s on stability, studies show
articles.title_zh: China’s thorium-229 nuclear clock beats Vienna’s on stability, studies show
articles.content_orig:
Chinese and European teams in ‘fierce but friendly’ competition to develop the next-generation timepieces
Initial results from the world’s first two working nuclear clocks indicate that China’s timepiece is about six times as stable as the one in Vienna, according to papers published this week by the journal Nature.
The clocks were developed independently but both the Chinese team, led by Tsinghua University in Beijing, and the researchers at Vienna’s TU Wien used thorium-229 nuclei embedded in crystals to keep time by the steady rhythm of the atom’s core, rather than the electrons whirling around it, as in atomic clocks.
When Nature reported in June that the two teams had separately developed the radical new devices, Thorsten Schumm, a member of the European team, said that “now we have a fierce but friendly global competition”.
According to the latest papers, the Beijing scientists also showed that two crystals grown separately kept the same time – a sign such clocks could be reliably reproduced, they said. Meanwhile, the Vienna team used its clock to hunt for dark matter, without success.

Lamarre-Condon has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Sydney in February 2024
Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast
A detective has broken down in court while describing the moment she found the bodies of two men allegedly murdered by former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon.
Jesse Baird, 26, and his new boyfriend Luke Davies, 29, were shot dead in a Sydney terrace in February 2024.
Lamarre-Condon, Baird’s ex and a then-police officer, has pleaded not guilty to murder, arguing the men died in two separate violent struggles after he entered the home disguised as a food delivery rider.
His subsequent efforts to dispose of their bodies at Bungonia – 200km south of Sydney – were indicative of his panic about the unexpected deaths, his lawyer has said.
A detective who co-ordinated a search of Cella Farm, where Lamarre-Condon allegedly tried unsuccessfully to sink the bodies in a dam, told the alleged murderer’s trial how she eventually found the remains of the two slain men eight days after the shooting.
Detective Senior Constable Christine Abela had been involved in searching the farm, where crime scene officers discovered a padlock had been cut, the jury heard.
Prosecutors allege the lock was cut with an angle grinder Lamarre-Condon had asked his friend to buy on the drive from Sydney.
Concrete blocks and gym weights were found at the edge of a dam on the farm, the jury was told.
On 27 February, Abela was diverted to a Greek monastery about 20km away.
“There was a strong smell as soon as I got out of the car,” she told a NSW supreme court jury on Wednesday.
“The scent of a decomposing body.”
The detective became emotional as prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC took her through her memories of the odour becoming stronger as she approached two blue and silver surfboard bags.
The bags were covered with sticks, branches and stones, the detective said.
The prosecution alleges Lamarre-Condon became infatuated with Baird after they broke off contact in November 2023, resolving to murder him.
However, Lamarre-Condon’s close friend Nicole Harvell told the court on Wednesday she could not remember any conversation with the ex-officer about Baird after the pair broke up for the final time.
That was despite her being in almost daily contact with the now-31-year-old.
after newsletter promotion
Senior Constable Harvell recalled trying to contact her friend when she saw media reports that he was under suspicion for the two men’s deaths.
“Fuck Beau, are you ok?” she texted to Lamarre-Condon’s phone.
She never received a reply.
The sworn officer maintained under cross-examination the accused killer had months earlier told her about enlisting his mother to help him lie to Baird.
Lamarre-Condon posted an Instagram story with a bunch of flowers and the caption: “When he’s in Melbourne but still sends you these.”
But publication was restricted to select friends that did not include Baird.
The photo was designed to imply Baird sent flowers to the accused, despite the pair not being in a relationship at the time, Harvell said.
When Baird discovered the ruse, Lamarre-Condon spent $160 on a bouquet identical to the photo to lie to Baird, the officer’s friend said.
Lamarre-Condon then sent a photo to Baird showing his mother with the fresh bouquet.
The bouquet had a handwritten note to imply his mother had been the intended recipient and they were from her partner, who was in Melbourne, the jury heard.
“I recall the accused telling me his mother had written that note,” Harvell said.

articles.title_zh: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
articles.content_orig:
Protests show no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed, and more marches planned for Thursday
The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boy’s hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters’ accusations of police brutality.
Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday.
The ‌wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron.
At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school.

articles.title_orig: World leaders solemnly mark 3 years since Oct. 7, as Hamas and Iran celebrate anniversary
articles.title_zh: World leaders solemnly mark 3 years since Oct. 7, as Hamas and Iran celebrate anniversary
articles.content_orig:
The Nova music festival memorial site on Oct. 07, 2026.
The world changed when Hamas attacked Israelis on Oct. 7, 2023 , catalyzing devastating conflict throughout the region . But within Israel, political sentiments have changed surprisingly little.
To some, the attack fulfilled long-term right-wing warnings that Israel’s withdrawal from Gaza would yield disaster; and the attack was incontrovertible proof that Palestinians will never live in peace with Israel.
Israeli left-wingers, for their part, have long held that a festering military rule over Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza, and failure to reach peace, would inevitably lead to violent conflagration. For them, Oct. 7 only proved that they had been right all along.
The standoff raises crucial questions. In three years since Oct. 7, how has the attack changed Israeli society? And how will the answer affect upcoming elections in Israel?
To be sure, there have been cataclysmic changes in Israel, and the Middle East at large, since Oct. 7. The war in Gaza that began that day has become Israel’s longest war. A relatively stable ceasefire with Lebanon from 2006 to 2023 ended when Hezbollah, a Shi’a militia group, fired on Israel the day after Hamas’ attack; after multiple escalations since then, the current ceasefire is precarious. Israel and the U.S. have waged two full-blown wars with Iran, and the Middle East is still threatened by spin-off conflicts.
The losses Israelis suffered on Oct. 7 and since then have affected the country collectively and profoundly. For two years, many Israelis went from demonstration to demonstration demanding that their government prioritize a deal with Hamas to release Israeli hostages. Hundreds of thousands have spent the last three years in and out of active reserve duty.
Since 2023, Israel has seen record levels of emigration and growing international isolation. Sixty-one percent of Israelis told pollsters for the Israel Democracy Institute (IDI) that the national mood is poor .
Moreover, the destruction of Palestinian life and society , still ongoing , will one day force a terrible reckoning within Israel.
What’s less visible, and more surprising, is what has stayed the same. Israelis’ attitudes towards Palestinians, occupation, and conflict have become more extreme. But I would argue that Israeli public opinion today says much more about how Israel had changed prior to Oct. 7. The change in national attitudes since that fateful day has been moderate and consistent with what came before.
In December 2022, almost a year before Oct. 7, support for peace through a two-state solution hit a historic low. In the joint Palestinian-Israeli survey I conduct together with colleagues at Tel Aviv University and the Palestinian Center for Policy and Survey Research, support stood at 39% of Israelis that year—the lowest since the 1990s. Among Jewish respondents, just 34% supported a two-state solution, and 37% believed Israel should permanently annex the West Bank while Palestinians would have limited rights.
When we conducted the study again in mid-2024, Jews were twice as likely to support a single, Israeli-dominated unequal state as they were to support two states.
Palestinian attitudes in 2022 were similar. Just one-third supported two states. Both sides showed a mirror-image majority who distrusted the other. In surveys by the IDI from that same time, 59% of Jewish Israelis defined themselves as right-wing; just 12% said they were left-wing.
What changed after Oct. 7? This July, the Tel Aviv University Peace Index survey found that support for two states stood at 31%, an eight-point decline in the four years since 2022. Now, IDI surveys find that just over 60% of Israeli Jews describe themselves as right-wing, just a few points higher than late 2022.
Israel has changed, but this change began years before Oct. 7 2023. In 2010 , no fewer than 71% of Israelis supported a two-state solution in the joint surveys. The years that followed were plagued by stagnation and dissipation of any peace process, regular wars with Hamas, and a heavily nationalist government in Israel. It stands to reason that these phenomena pushed Israeli society further to the right. Support for the two-state solution eroded slowly, then rapidly by the end of the decade.
That shift was self-reinforcing: the more right-wing Israelis became (primarily the Jewish population), the more elected leaders took ever-more radical positions such as supporting settlement expansion and de facto annexation in the West Bank. In 2019, Prime Minister Netanyahu began referring to extending sovereignty over parts of the West Bank, or de jure annexation . The current government accelerated those processes drastically.
Study after study shows that Arab citizens of Israel have remained the strongest supporters of peace, before and after the current wars. But with Jewish Israeli and Palestinian attitudes so dismal in the years before Oct. 7, the chances of resurgent violence almost seemed inevitable.
In other words, most Israelis did not radically transform their worldview after Oct. 7. In fact, hardline political trends were among the many factors contributing to the terrible escalation to begin with.
Another thing that hasn’t changed in Israel during the last three years of war: hopes for peace. The number of Israeli Jews who self-describe as left-wing has barely shifted. In a May survey for the Institute for National Security Studies, about 20% of the total population, Jews and Arabs, define themselves as left-wing, and a similar share typically say they are centrist. These groups embrace a commitment to democracy, liberal values, separation of religion and state, and reject the religious fundamentalism of the current government.
The left remains committed to peace via diplomacy and Palestinian self-determination. In a mid-2025 survey I conducted for a peace organization called A Land for All, where I am also an active member, the large majority of self-defined left-wing Israelis, and nearly half of centrists, supported a basic two-state solution.
Do peace attitudes even matter, when there is no peace process? That may be theoretical for now, but elections aren’t. Israelis will be voting on Oct. 27. Polls show the voters deeply divided , just as they were in the elections held between 2019 and 2022.
Netanyahu’s far-right coalition is not doing well. Nearly all polls show his coalition parties well below their actual result in 2022. And most mainstream polls show a consistent majority for today’s opposition parties.
At first glance, these shifts might seem antithetical. Aren’t these ideological and electoral trends moving in contradictory directions: more right-wing, but a majority against the current government?
It turns out that even the Israeli electoral contradiction is not new. During the five elections from 2019 through 2022, a majority of Israelis were right-wing and voted for right-wing parties. But to form a coalition, some of those parties no longer supported Netanyahu and refused to join a coalition under his leadership. Netanyahu therefore commanded only about half the seats in parliament following four of these cycles. Neither side had a clear or firm coalition majority, and the country was thrown into electoral turmoil five times over.
But if all mainstream polls show the anti-Netanyahu parties winning, including right-wing opposition parties, shouldn’t that mean a decisive outcome against him this time? Not quite: no poll shows Israel’s Jewish, Zionist parties reaching a majority in October.

articles.title_orig: Stock market today: Dow falls 500 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq retreat from records as Treasury yields hit 24-year high
articles.title_zh: Stock market today: Dow falls 500 points, S&P 500 and Nasdaq retreat from records as Treasury yields hit 24-year high
articles.content_orig:
U.S. Treasury yields came off their highs after a solid sale of 10-year notes. Earlier, the 10-year yield rose to its highest level in more than two decades.
The 10-year Treasury last traded around 3 basis points higher at 5.288%. Earlier in the session, it reached 5.35%, its highest level since 2002. The 30-year Treasury bond yield also traded below a 24-year high, at 5.67%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
The Treasury sold $39 billion of 10-year notes in an auction on Wednesday. According to BMO, the sale was "strong", with higher than average bidding from non-dealers.
Indirect bidders, which include global central banks, took 80.3% of the auction — above a 10-auction average of 72.4%. Direct bidders, scooped up 17.1% of the sale, just below an average of 18.3%. Dealers, meanwhile, bought just 2.5% of the notes offered, well below a 9.4% mean.
"The 24-year highs in rates brought out the buyers and resulted in a great auction," said Peter Boockvar, market strategist and author of The Boock Report.
Nonetheless, it still was the highest auction yield since 2000 at 5.3%.
This was the second of three Treasury Department sales this week. The government sold $58 billion in 3-year notes on Tuesday and is scheduled to sell $22 billion 30-year bonds on Thursday.
Treasury also will stage its latest buyback operation on Thursday, when it will be targeting maturities between 20 years and 30 years. The liquidity support operation will be at least $4 billion, or double the normal size. The last buyback in that range came to just over $4 billion.
Bonds have been selling off recently with investors concerned about inflation and rising energy prices. The 10-year has surged 60 basis points since the end of July, while U.S. crude prices have soared 20% in that time.
Selling pressure is also picking up overseas. The yield on the 10-year French bond surged 12 basis points to trade at 4.876%. The 10-year U.K. Gilt yield jumped 7 basis points to 5.447%.
Against that backdrop, FOMC meeting minutes were released, showing central bank officials expect to hike rates further — but gave no indication as to when .
"With regard to the outlook for monetary policy beyond the current meeting, most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end," the summary of the Fed's September meeting stated.

articles.title_zh: Rare World War II aircraft on display in Huntsville
articles.content_orig:
HUNTSVILLE, Ala. ( WAFF ) - A rare piece of World War II history is in Huntsville today. The B-29 Superfortress known as Doc is at Huntsville’s airport as part of a tour stop this week.
Doc is one of only two B-29s still flying today. More than 1,600 were built in Wichita during the war.
It is joined by a P-51 Mustang. Those are rare too. Only about 150 of them are still around.
Visitors got a chance to see the aircraft up close and learn about the crews who designed, built and flew them.
“It’s a pretty special opportunity...really makes the history jump off the page,” Josh Wells said.
Wells said the event also helps younger generations understand an important piece of history.

articles.title_orig: Parliament calls for principled EU-China policy that combines dialogue, fair trade, and human rights
articles.title_zh: Parliament calls for principled EU-China policy that combines dialogue, fair trade, and human rights
articles.content_orig:
The European Parliament has advocated establishing a stronger, more principled EU-China policy that balances dialogue with the promotion of European interests. In a recommendation approved on Wednesday by a vote of 454 in favour, 86 against, and 110 abstentions, Members of the European Parliament (MEPs) highlighted the EU’s commitment to fostering a multilateral world. They underscored the importance of engaging with China on pressing global challenges, including peace and security, climate change, and human rights.
At the same time, MEPs acknowledged that bilateral relations have reached a critical juncture, largely due to China’s unfair economic practices and its position concerning Russia’s war against Ukraine. They expressed substantial concern over verified reports indicating that the Chinese military has trained Russian military personnel for involvement in Ukraine.
MEPs contend that the EU should work closely with the United States, G7 partners, and other like-minded nations to encourage China to use its influence over Russia to help end the conflict.
“Today’s majority marks a turning point in Europe’s China policy. With this week’s Franco-German initiative, a broad EU consensus is emerging on the need for a more balanced economic relationship with China. I hope Commissioner Šefčovič will take this united economic message to Beijing tomorrow. But this report goes even further: we want cooperation with China where possible, while standing firm on our security and values. As long as fundamental differences persist, systemic rivalry will also be part of our relationship,” rapporteur Hilde Vautmans (Renew, BE) said.
Direct engagement between the European Parliament and Chinese authorities resumed last year, after a suspension that began in 2021 when the Chinese government imposed sanctions on several MEPs in response to the EU’s human rights sanctions against certain Chinese officials and organisations. Between March and June 2026, three parliamentary delegations visited China, with a fourth visit scheduled for later in October 2026.
MEPs emphasised the urgent need to address the potential risks associated with the EU’s economic dependency on China. They called for a comprehensive de-risking strategy that focuses on critical raw materials, pharmaceuticals, batteries, electric vehicles, information and communication technology, semiconductors, and other strategic sectors. The Parliament has also called for enhanced investment screening and protection of vital technologies, infrastructure, and supply chains.
Furthermore, MEPs identified several challenges facing the EU economy, such as China’s industrial overcapacity, state subsidies, and barriers limiting European firms’ access to the Chinese market. They have called for reciprocity and a level playing field in trade and investment, supporting balanced EU actions when China does not adequately open its markets. They also advocated strengthening Global Gateway partnerships to provide a credible alternative to China’s Belt and Road Initiative, especially in Africa and Latin America.
The report reaffirms the EU’s One China policy and opposes any unilateral changes to the status quo in Taiwan through force or coercion. MEPs called for heightened resilience against cyber threats, foreign interference, espionage, and hybrid challenges, while also demanding a reinforced human rights dialogue with China focused on issues such as repression, forced labour, and policies in Tibet and Xinjiang.
The Parliament expressed significant concern about the recent adoption of the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress and its potential to entrench assimilationist policies further. They also called for the unconditional release of political prisoners.

articles.title_orig: New Production of Lord of the Rings Musical to Embark on World Tour
articles.title_zh: New Production of Lord of the Rings Musical to Embark on World Tour
articles.content_orig:
This new production will be directed by Bruce Guthrie.
October 07, 2026 By Diep Tran
The road goes ever on, especially if you're a Lord of the Rings musical. A new stage production called The Lord of the Rings – The Epic Stage Adventure will world premiere at the Zorlu Performing Arts Center in Istanbul October 8, 2027. Further touring stops will include Bucharest, Prague, Warsaw, Thessaloniki, Tallinn, Athens, Sofia, Zagreb, and Dubai, with more (including venues in Europe) to be announced.
Based on J.R.R. Tolkien's fantasy novels, the new production will be directed by Bruce Guthrie, head of film and theatre at the National Centre for Performing Arts, Mumbai. It will feature scenic, video, and puppetry design by Tony and Olivier Award winner Andrzej Goulding ( Life of Pi ), and a score by Academy Award winner A.R. Rahman , the Finnish folk group Värttinä, and Tony Award Winner Christopher Nightingale, with book and lyrics by Shaun McKenna and Matthew Warchus .
It follows the hobbit Frodo as he embarks on a quest—alongside a fellowship composed of an elf, a dwarf, some men, and other hobbits—to destroy the One Ring and save Middle Earth.
The Lord of the Rings stage musical first premiered in 2006 at Princess of Wales Theatre in Toronto, before opening in the West End in 2007 at Theatre Royal, Drury Lane. A well-received production, which originated in 2023 at the Watermill Theatre in the U.K. just finished a North American and international tour. The forthcoming touring production features a new creative team.
Lord of the Rings is is produced by Kevin Wallace and William Bennett for KW Productions, George Isaak for People Entertainment Group, and Middle-earth Enterprises, LLC, with Peter Huntley and Callum Runciman as executive producers and general managers for Smart Entertainment.
Tickets for the Istanbul engagement will be available at Zorlupsm.com .

articles.title_orig: China’s High-Tech Ambitions Have a Blue-Collar Status Problem - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: China’s High-Tech Ambitions Have a Blue-Collar Status Problem - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
As China celebrated its dominance at the Asian Games that concluded days ago in Nagoya, Japan, its achievement at another global sporting festival in Shanghai has been largely overlooked. In the 2026 edition of WorldSkills, what the organizers call an Olympics for vocational skills, the Chinese team topped the medal table with 41 gold, 11 silver, and 4 bronze medals. In fact, the Chinese team has topped the medal table five straight times in the biennial competition, a phenomenon that has been attributed to the country’s unparalleled investments in providing systematic coaching and training for athletes in the same way it does for the regular Olympics.
Beyond simply winning medals, the Chinese authorities felt the need to drum up public interest in the competition. Local and national media , and even governments , covered WorldSkills extensively while it largely went unnoticed in other countries. Given that whatever prestige that China earns from WorldSkills is largely geared toward a domestic audience rather than an international one, it begs the question of why China would even bother with prompting something that leads to little gain in global stature.
The answer to the question may be found in a February 2026 announcement from the Chinese Ministry of Education (MoE) suggesting vocational school reforms. The document criticized the current system’s lack of connection between education and employers, producing few skilled industrial workers essential for driving China’s next generation of high-tech manufacturing.
China’s 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan emphasized that manufacturing remains central in ensuring the technological self-sufficiency underlying long-term economic growth and safeguarding national security. The MoE implied that the country’s vocational schools, without reforms, would be incapable of producing the human resources needed to achieve that goal.
But for vocational schools to urgently produce talent for high-tech manufacturing, they need more than just an appropriate curriculum. They also need the best raw talent that China has to offer. Here is where vocational schools fall short.
China’s university enrollment increased from 1 million in 1999 to 9.6 million in 2020. The country’s brightest increasingly aspire to join the ranks of what used to be a tiny segment of the intellectual elite signaled by a university diploma. The expanding path toward college education has cemented a social hierarchy in which a bachelor’s degree followed by white-collar work is seen as more desirable than a vocational one followed by a career in manual labor, no matter how technically sophisticated.
That norm of high-education aspirations is most clearly seen in study abroad. My primary job as a college admissions consultant leads me to interact with hundreds of Chinese families who are first and foremost attracted to higher-ranked institutions with well-recognized names. In choosing between the likes of the American Ivy Leagues and the British Oxbridge, they care less about what practical skills they can acquire, but whether the degrees indicate a highly competitive environment, and by proxy, the intelligence of successful applicants. Despite much cheaper costs and clear paths for employment, very few indicate interest in English-language higher-education programs in Germany and other European countries anchored by technical apprenticeships.
It is this cultural norm that the MoE must fight against as it seeks to overhaul the vocational school system in China. The proposed collaboration with major manufacturers will help. In a slowing economy, many applicants may be interested in blue-collar work with the likes of Huawei and Xiaomi, rather than a bachelor’s degree that comes with unemployment afterwards. But without changing the cultural norms of seeing technical education as “lower” than the university one, vocational schools in China, no matter how reformed, can still only attract those who are not afraid to be seen as desperate and obtuse enough to work on the factory floor.
Hence the glowing coverage of WorldSkills. The prestige of China’s medalists is about bringing pride not just to the country, but to their professions. And to further bestow status, China is turning hundreds of vocational schools into diploma-granting colleges, slapping bachelor’s degrees on vocational training. If better prospects for jobs do not bring brighter talent into technical education, the hope is that erasing the difference in visual appearance between universities and vocational schools can break down the hierarchical thinking.
It remains to be seen whether China’s dwindling ranks of youngsters will be sufficiently lured by the more attractive job prospects offered by manufacturing. As Chinese firms wow domestic and foreign audiences with fully automated dark factories, the image of grittiness associated with manufacturing is being chipped away. But will that overcome an ingrained educational culture that sees the work of the brain as higher in social status as that of the hand, even if the hand is increasingly replaced by robotics? It will depend on whether the Chinese mentality will evolve as fast as the country’s approach to industrial policies and technologies.

articles.title_orig: World News in Brief: Child migrants in Europe, Greenland forced contraception scandal, FAO hunger updates
articles.title_zh: World News in Brief: Child migrants in Europe, Greenland forced contraception scandal, FAO hunger updates
articles.content_orig:
Facebook Twitter Print Email
New data on child migrants published on Wednesday highlighted the harrowing treatment many face while travelling to Europe in search of work and shelter.
Just over 31,000 children arrived in Greece, Italy, Spain, Bulgaria and Malta last year – 25 per cent less than in 2024.
Of more than 4,600 teenagers and young adults aged 15 to 24 surveyed, nearly half reported suffering physical violence.
One of the main routes migrants take today is the through the central Mediterranean from Libya and Tunisia in northern Africa to Italy, according to the UN migration agency, IOM .
IOM spokesperson Kennedy Omondi said there has to be stronger cooperation between European countries and those along migration routes to protect children travelling alone.
“The latest data in our report shows how vulnerable children are subjected to violence and exploitation when safe pathways are limited and they are forced to rely on smugglers,” the spokesperson said.
Among the adolescents and young adults who made the journey, 28 per cent said they had been held against their will and 17 per cent said they had been forced into work. Almost eight in 10 are male.
One 19-year-old migrant worker from Bangladesh cited in the report said his boss in Libya took away his passport and forced him into slave labour, hitting him when he was considered not to be working hard enough.
A 20-year-old woman from Liberia said she arrived in Algeria where she was raped and forced to work as a cleaner. Seven months’ pregnant, she escaped on a boat to Spain.
Most cases of abuse occurred in Libya, according to IOM. More than 20,000 of the 31,100 children who reached Europe along mixed migration routes last year arrived without a parent or guardian, according to a joint report with the UN Children’s Fund ( UNICEF ) and refugee agency, UNHCR .
IOM Director General Amy Pope called for stronger cooperation between European countries and States along migration routes to protect children travelling alone. Ms. Pope also called for action to tackle the smuggling and criminal networks that exploit them.
Independent UN human rights experts have warned that attempts to downplay the forced contraception of thousands of Inuit women and girls in Greenland threaten any prospect of genuine redress.
The concerns follow a dissenting report by two former members of an expert group appointed by Greenland’s Government.
It concluded there were no empirical grounds to assume that Danish or Greenlandic authorities intentionally and systematically inserted intrauterine devices without consent.
The two governments have already recognised that the Indigenous women and girls endured the practice for decades in public care institutions and have apologised.
But, the independent experts – who receive no salary for their work and are not UN staff – said true remedy cannot be achieved without “a clear, accurate and undisputed record of historical facts”.
They urged Denmark to make compensation schemes more accessible linguistically and culturally, ensure women with disabilities are not forgotten and address wider abuses such as forced adoption and the removal of Inuit children from their parents.
“Their dignity, voices and rights must remain at the centre of all efforts toward truth, justice, healing and reconciliation,” the Human Rights Council -appointed experts said.
The UN Food and Agriculture Organization ( FAO ) has called for urgent funding to help families in the Near East and North Africa to keep growing food and earning a living as conflict, displacement and climate pressures deepen hunger.
More than 45 million people across the region face crisis-level hunger or worse.
At the same time, funding shortfalls are limiting support to protect food production.
In Sudan, where 19.5 million people face high levels of acute food insecurity, only 23 per cent of the $193 million needed under the 2026–2028 emergency response plan has been funded. In Yemen, FAO has secured less than one per cent of the $87.9 million it requires for 2027.
In Lebanon, more than one million people were displaced after the March 2026 escalation, and more than 22 per cent of agricultural land has reportedly been damaged.
“Investing early in seeds, livestock, water and other agricultural support can protect livelihoods, prevent hunger from deepening and reduce humanitarian needs over time,” said FAO Deputy Director-General Beth Bechdol.

articles.title_orig: Asia Focus: Expanding Global Reach, World's Most Populous Continent Continues To Flourish
articles.title_zh: Asia Focus: Expanding Global Reach, World's Most Populous Continent Continues To Flourish
articles.content_orig:
Get Pollstar News and more delivered right to your inbox with Pollstar Daily Pulse.
By signing up, you agree to Pollstar’s Privacy Policy and Terms of Use
The Asian touring market continues to thrive, with promoters and venues reaping the rewards of artists both homegrown and international presenting top-notch concert productions at home and abroad, with new partnerships and long-lasting relationships behind the scenes meaning the traffic is both inbound as well as exported to the rest of the world.
The dominance of K-pop in the region, anchored by activity in Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Indonesia and Dubai, continues. The top four touring acts, as reported to Pollstar (see page 162), were K-pop bands, with SEVENTEEN showing the way with a gross of $97,394,005. TWICE grossed $76,176,781 and TOMORROW X TOGETHER did $53,035,381. Ranked No. 4, Korean powerhouse BTS grossed $49,069,994 in Asia as part of its mammoth “ARIRANG” world tour, which was No. 1 on Pollstar ’s Q3 chart. Those shows were the chart-topping boy band’s first in nearly four years due to military service.
Western acts were busy as well, with Lady Gaga leading the charge ($44,379,794 grossed), fifth overall in the territory, and Travis Scott was close behind ($37,922,441). Just to reinforce the Asian presence in the home region, G.E.M. came in seventh ($31,725,779), BLACKPINK is eighth ($29,193,966 grossed) and ENHYPEN nabbed the ninth spot ($21,562,532 grossed).
The key players in the region who Pollstar talked to were uniformly enthusiastic about business. HYBE was the leading promoter in the region with $247,965,087 in gross revenue. HYBE 360 President Yoojin Oh (Impact Honoree, see page 176), who oversees the company’s concert business, says, “Over the past year, HYBE artists’ global tours have continued to expand not only in scale but also in the breadth of markets they reach.”
Japan’s presence as the longtime leader in the Asian music industry remained strong. Three of the top five promotion agencies were Japanese and the country held six of the top 10 spots. The biggest player in the nation was Creativeman Productions, with $103,665,840 in gross revenue, third overall in Pollstar ’s Asia chart. Naoki Shimizu, president of the promoter behind the long-running Summer Sonic festival, notes, “The live music market has bounced back from the pandemic and is expanding even more than before.” Of Japan in particular, he says, “The breadth of the entertainment landscape is a key factor. There is a capacity to turn anything — whether local acts, Asian artists, Western music, anime, or voice actors — into a major live concert market.” In second place for promoters was Live Nation with $209,803,871 in gross revenue reported.
Dennis Argenzia, president of global touring, Asia-Pacific at Live Nation, has observed a shift in enthusiasm from artists. “Asia is at a really exciting point in its evolution as a live music market,” Argenzia says. “For many years, we had to convince artists and their teams to come to Asia — today, the conversation is very different. Artists want to perform here because they see the growth in demand and the opportunity to build deeper connections with fans across the region.”
Hong Kong appears as a microcosm of the expanding Asia market. The 50,000- capacity Kai Tak Stadium is a crucial venue for all of Asia. Kath Wong, senior manager at the firm that runs the stadium, emphasizes the outsized role K-pop plays in Asia touring and Hong Kong’s place in the market, with concert highlights from BLACKPINK and SEVENTEEN at Kai Tak Stadium.
“Each show serves as a milestone not only for Kai Tak Sports Park, but for Hong Kong as a whole,” Wong says. “It demonstrated that the stadium could host some of the world’s biggest touring artists and deliver complex international production to the standard expected by the artist, promoter and production teams.”
She expands on the environment, with Kai Tak Sports Park including both the 50,000-seat stadium with a retractable roof and the indoor Kai Tak Arena, which can accommodate 10,000 people and has 80% retractable seating.
Irene Chan, CEO of AsiaWorld-Expo, which operates the 14,000-cap arena of the same name in Hong Kong (the third biggest in Asia), is extremely upbeat on the business in 2026: “Audiences increasingly seek destination events that combine music, culture, fashion, art, retail, food and technology—driving the global trend of ‘festivalisation’ and creating new revenue and partnership opportunities beyond ticket sales.”
Global promoter AEG Presents, based in the U.S., is also focused on the region. Adam Wilkes, president and CEO of AEG Presents Europe and Asia-Pacific, who has worked in the Asian touring market for decades, offers a comprehensive overview.
“Asia is already a core part of the global touring ecosystem, and its significance will only grow,” he says. “International artists are reaching more markets, supported by a wave of world-class venues – both newly opened and under construction. The regional touring industry is also becoming more sophisticated, allowing artists to build meaningful careers across multiple countries rather than only at home.”
He adds that the world environment has changed, catapulting Asia to a new position. “Crucially, the traffic now moves both ways,” he says. “K-pop led the way, but Japanese, Chinese and Indian artists are increasingly finding audiences and performing at the highest level around the world. More inbound touring, better infrastructure and a growing pipeline of internationally successful Asian talent make the potential enormous.”
In Japan, Shimizu reflects on Creativeman’s successes but also looks forward.
“After Summer Sonic, the biggest tour of the year for us would be Iron Maiden,” he says of the globally renowned heavy metal pioneers. Other rock bands continue to show strength in the market. “Last year, it was Green Day, and Radiohead is coming up next year. It is a joy, after such a long career, to have tours every year by bands I’ve promoted for over two decades.”
The company is set to expand its dominant network even further. Shimizu explains, “Creativeman recently entered into a strategic partnership with AEG. In the past, artists like Taylor Swift, Justin Bieber and Ariana Grande have started out working with Creativeman for their Japan shows, only to move on to global tours handled by others. Now, however, we have a setting where we can continue working with them throughout that process. Furthermore, Creativeman’s 36 year-career will undoubtedly bring added value to AEG.”
Kaori Hayashi, president of Live Nation H.I.P. (Hayashi International Promotions), notes the promoter is set for a banner year. “We are seeing strong demand for live entertainment in Japan. More artists are touring, more live events are taking place, and more fans are attending these events. Bruno Mars’ 12-show dome tour in January 2027 will be the largest tour ever undertaken by an international artist in Japan. It will span six cities across the country – from Osaka to Nagoya – reflecting the depth of demand for international artists well beyond Tokyo, and is another indication of the scale of opportunity in this market.”
The 37,000-cap GMO Arena Saitama (formerly Saitama Super Arena), one of Japan’s biggest arenas and the second largest in Asia, has been closed for a major renovation since January. Operations will resume in April 2027, and Yutaka Minagawa, MD of the arena, tells Pollstar they have already secured a number of major international artist performances.
“Japan’s music market continues to benefit from strong and stable demand for domestic artists, particularly within the J-Pop genre,” Minagawa says. “In addition to J-Pop, K-Pop enjoys enduring popularity, while major international artists continue to include Japan as part of their world tours. This creates a highly diverse live entertainment ecosystem where multiple genres can successfully coexist.”

articles.title_zh: Shia LaBeouf’s wife Mia Goth files for divorce amid his legal turmoil
articles.content_orig:
Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf after 10 years of marriage.
The Pearl star, 32, filed the papers Tuesday night and cited "irreconcilable differences" as the reason, according to TMZ .
Although they have been legally married since October 2016, the former couple had a turbulent on-and-off relationship in the public eye for over a decade. After Goth and LaBeouf met on the set of Nymphomaniac: Vol. II in 2012, they tied the knot in Las Vegas in 2016 and broke up two years later. They then reconciled around 2020 and welcomed their daughter, Isabel, in 2022. Their date of separation is listed on the documents as July 28, 2025.
Goth is asking for primary legal and physical custody of Isabel, and is requesting to terminate the court's ability to award spousal support to either of the actors.
The Independent has reached out to representatives for Goth and LaBeouf for comment.
Mia Goth has filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf (Getty)
LaBeouf and Goth have been separated for over a year, court documents revealed (Getty)
News of the filing comes just one day after LaBeouf's ex-girlfriend, singer FKA twigs, settled a lawsuit against the 40-year-old Megalopolis actor , meaning she is now free to speak about her alleged experiences of sexual abuse with him.
The lawsuit was settled after LaBeouf agreed to end the nondisclosure provisions from the former couple's settlement in December 2025.
Their long legal fight started in 2020, when Twigs accused LaBeouf of being sexually, mentally and physically abusive throughout their relationship, which lasted for about nine months in 2018. LaBeouf denied the allegations at the time.
The singer's attorney, Mathew Rosengart, said Wednesday in a statement shared with The Independent : "On the heels of Mr. LaBeouf's now dismissed, failed December 2025 arbitration against Twigs in which he sought money from her, this important victory completely frees her to discuss her experience, advocate for other women who might be less privileged, and freely support the charitable causes of her choice, which she was previously blocked from doing. To her great credit, Twigs stood up for something larger than herself, all female survivors of sexual abuse."
LaBeouf's attorney, Shawn Holley, said that the former Disney Channel star "wishes Twigs nothing but the best in her life and career and, to that end, has agreed to end their long-standing dispute."
"Twigs has spoken about this matter for years and there is now nothing to prevent her from continuing to do so," Holley told The Independent . She refused to comment on Goth's filing.
Singer FKA twigs settled a lawsuit against ex-boyfriend Shia LaBeouf earlier this week (Getty)
LaBeouf is currently on probation after he was arrested after getting into a drunken brawl in New Orleans in February. He pleaded guilty to misdemeanor battery charges in June and was sentenced to two years' probation, rehabilitation for alcohol abuse, sensitivity training and anger management classes.
The actor had moved to the Louisiana city after his separation from Goth, Page Six reported at the time.
In March, he spoke about his breakup with Goth in an interview on Channel 5 With Andrew Callaghan.
"We were deeply unhappy," LaBeouf said. "I made a lot of mistakes early on before we tried to have a baby. I had violated trust in a big, big way."
He said that their problems were "impossible" to fix, but that he still had love and respect for Goth. "We're in a good spot. I mean, this isn't new," he said. "We've been there for a while, we're trying to figure out co-parenting, and we're good. Even through all this, she gives me grace."

articles.title_orig: How PvP Progression in World of Warcraft: Forever Works
articles.title_zh: How PvP Progression in World of Warcraft: Forever Works
articles.content_orig:
Whether you’re charging into battlegrounds with your faction or setting your sights on long-term PvP (Player vs. Player) goals, World of Warcraft: Forever brings a refreshed sense of purpose to every match-up. This approach gives players more reasons to take part throughout the season while preserving the spirit of competition that defined PvP in the original World of Warcraft .
When reimagining the PvP system, we wanted to keep the design pillar of “Approachable and Familiar” firmly in view: simplifying the original Honor System while staying true to its roots.
In World of Warcraft: Forever, PvP progression has two parts: Honor and Rank Points.
Honor is a currency players earn through taking part in PvP content. This includes defeating other players, completing battlegrounds, and finishing relevant PvP quests. Players also earn increased Honor in highlighted battlegrounds during their holiday weeks.
As part of these updates, we reviewed Honor gains across battlegrounds so acquisition rates are more consistent across the board. We want players to enjoy the full range of battleground maps without feeling compelled to choose Alterac Valley solely for Honor efficiency.
Rank Points come from PvP activities such as battlegrounds and relevant PvP quests, with holiday-week battlegrounds offering an additional boost. As players earn Rank Points, they advance through familiar PvP ranks from original World of Warcraft, working toward the ultimate titles of High Warlord for the Horde or Grand Marshal for the Alliance. Ranks have a weekly cap, retaining the foundation of the original system while making the journey more accessible.
Honor can be used to purchase two sets of PvP gear: one blue-quality set and one epic-quality set. The epic set requires the blue piece plus an Emboldened Seal to upgrade it, and Emboldened Seals have rank requirements players must reach before purchasing. There are also new and reworked items to fill gaps for specializations that were previously missing options. For example, Shaman now have healer, melee, and caster PvP gear sets they can acquire.
Below are the rank requirements for PvP item rewards:
Rank 1 - Tabard Rank 2 - PvP Trinket Rank 3 - Cloaks Rank 4 - Necklace Rank 5 - Combat Potions Rank 6 - Tabard Rank 7 - Battle Standard Rank 8 - Epic Bracers/Epic Belt Upgrade Token Rank 9 - Epic Boots Upgrade Token Rank 10 - Epic Gloves Upgrade Token Rank 11 - Mounts Rank 12 - Epic Legs/Epic Shoulders Upgrade Token Rank 13 - Epic Chest/Epic Helm Upgrade Token Rank 14 - Epic Weapons
To view your progress, you can open your Character Pane (Hotkey-C) then select the Player vs. Player tab on the right side of the interface. It will show you your rank, your current Rank Points, and what rewards are available for purchase based on your rank.
During a PvP season, players can progress through the ranks and earn Honor. Each season also includes a journey with weekly tasks to complete. Successfully completing those tasks grants Honor and Rank Points, and three tasks each season also grant a Legacy Point. Completing these tasks is part of the seasonal journey, and because they are tied to the Legacy System, they remain available to complete in future seasons.
With more ways to make progress each week and meaningful goals to pursue throughout the season, PvP in World of Warcraft: Forever gives players a clear path to jump in, compete, and keep building toward what comes next.

articles.title_orig: World's Oil Reserves 'Scarily Thin' As Houthi, Hormuz Attacks Push Oil Back Over $100 A Barrel
articles.title_zh: World's Oil Reserves 'Scarily Thin' As Houthi, Hormuz Attacks Push Oil Back Over $100 A Barrel
articles.content_orig:
Oil has definitely gotten more expensive since Republicans started their senseless war with Iran . But even if we're already paying over $6 a gallon for diesel , oil prices haven't risen nearly as much as they would have if countries around the world hadn't been pulling every lever at their disposal to keep prices in check, including releasing their petroleum stockpiles. That's given oil markets more of a cushion, but that may be about to change. According to Reuters , "industry executives," told an economic forum in London that global stockpiles are dwindling, raising the risk that fuel prices may soon rise even further.
We've known for a while that the U.S. doesn't have much oil left in its strategic reserve. In addition to being close to the practical floor, frequently draining and refilling the caverns as previous administrations have done means continuing to release oil from the reserves risks irreparably damaging the caverns the oil is stored in . According to Yahoo Finance , however, that hasn't stopped Trump from announcing plans to release another 40 million barrels in the coming months. Apparently, the rest of the world isn't doing much better, either.
Speaking at this year's Energy ⁠Intelligence Forum in London, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said, "Less than ​6 billion barrels of commercial inventories remain today, with the vast majority not practically available, so the system is ​already straining." Unfortunately for all of us, the bad news doesn't stop there. As Reuters put it:
More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of ​this year's Middle East crisis, which was the last major tool in the box, Nasser said.
The International Energy Agency, the West's oil watchdog ​and coordinator of its strategic oil reserves, is preparing to release 100 million barrels of crude and diesel to help alleviate soaring diesel prices, but it is not clear if some of that total will include volumes from its record first 400 million barrel release in March that hadn't hit the market ​yet.
"It took a lot of negotiations, but it is 100 million," Nasser said of the IEA decision. "Inventories are reaching a stress level. ​Only 10% or less is available, that's why they struggle with 100 million barrels."
World oil demand is about 102 million barrels per day, according to ‌the IEA.
Releasing more oil from global reserves may keep price increases in check, but only temporarily. Once countries hit their practical floors, they'll be done. When that will happen exactly and how it would play out are still impossible to predict, but as countries around the world lose access to their main source of control over oil prices, the only direction left for them to go is up.
Nasser wasn't the only executive sounding the alarm about global oil reserves, either. Chevron CEO Mike Wirth told the forum that dwindling reserves threaten the stability of oil markets and set a higher price floor per barrel. Multiple speakers reportedly said they expect the volatility in the market to continue through 2027. They also said they believe it will be several years before global oil inventories finally reach pre-war levels again.
We aren't just burning through our oil stockpiles, either. Global natural gas reserves are also dwindling, and as Reuters wrote, "[a] bad winter could bring about a 'bloodbath' in the gas market in the first quarter of 2027 if storage hits minimal levels." So that's not great news. Sometimes witnessing a bloodbath is enjoyable, like that time Georgia beat TCU 65-7 in the 2023 men's college football national championship, but I don't get the feeling we'll have nearly as much fun if we're using "bloodbath" to describe the natural gas market.
Of course, we could all get back on the road to oil and gas market recovery a lot faster if the White House could just find a way to end the war. For months now, Republicans have been telling us Iran is desperate to make a deal, but no lasting peace deal has ever materialized. At least Trump's unelected son-in-law managed to line up some lucrative deals for himself. I mean, what's the point of starting a war if you can't enrich your family at the expense of everyone else in the country you run?
As you can probably imagine, talk like that hasn't been good for cheap oil. CNBC reports that Brent Crude is back over $100 a barrel after brief drop, while West Texas Intermediate is sitting just under $90 a barrel. And while Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman recently claimed repairs to its East-West pipeline have allowed the Gulf nation to begin moving 5.8 million barrels, they still haven't managed to stop attacks from Houthi rebels, and despite the U.S. military's best efforts, Iran continues to attack tankers traveling through the Strait of Hormuz. From CNBC:
However, concerns that there may be further supply disruptions in the Middle East weighed on sentiment. The Saudi aviation authority reportedly said Tuesday that the country's airports in Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks, amid growing hostilities between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom.
Iran's move to step up attacks on tankers which are transiting through the Strait of Hormuz has also led to renewed worries over oil supplies among traders, as it threatens to disrupt the fragile rebound in oil exports through the crucial waterway.
CNBC also spoke with Zaye Capital Markets CIO Naeem Aslam, who said the oil industry ""caught between improving physical supply and persistent geopolitical risk." Meanwhile, Samer Hasn, a senior market analyst at XS.com (a forex trading platform) told the news outlet, "The sustained ability of the Houthis in Yemen to target oil facilities hundreds of kilometers from the border keeps the risks of a renewed large-scale crude supply disruption present and high, and these risks could worsen if the Houthis feel the need to apply more pressure as a result of losing more territory."
Today, NBC News reports the Houthis continued their attacks, with their spokesperson, Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, claiming to have successfully hit Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport again. Saree didn't provide evidence to support that claim, but tracking data provided by Flightradar24 did show that flights were temporarily impacted. The Houthis also claim to have hit another airport, two Saudi military bases and an air base, and Yemen's port city of Aden, with a ballistic missile strike near the city's airport already confirmed.
The Saudi military, backed by allied in Yemen, has responded with both air and ground attacks in an attempt to loosen the Houthis' control on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. How successful they've been, however, still remains to be seen. Saudi officials have claimed to have taken back several key areas, but CBS News reports the Houthis dispute that claim. Whatever's going on, it sure doesn't sound like gas will get much cheaper anytime soon.

articles.title_orig: Modelo owner Constellation is getting creative to bring back beer drinkers as overall demand weakens
articles.title_zh: Modelo owner Constellation is getting creative to bring back beer drinkers as overall demand weakens
articles.content_orig:
Constellation Brands beat quarterly earnings and revenue expectations as its beer brands gained market share, but continued consumer caution tempered results.
As it navigates high food and fuel prices and choosy shoppers, Constellation is turning to special occasions and diversification to help drive sales.
The maker of Modelo Especial, Corona and Pacifico on Wednesday reported fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings of $3.74 per share on $2.63 billion in revenue, ahead of Wall Street estimates of $3.56 and $2.54 billion, respectively.
Beer revenue rose 5% to roughly $2.47 billion, while beer shipments increased 5.5%. However, the company said beer depletions, a measure of sales from distributors to retailers and other customers, declined slightly during the quarter, indicating consumer demand was softer than shipment demands suggest.
"We have spent much of the first half rebuilding distributor inventory levels," said Constellation Brands CEO Nicholas Fink on the company's earnings call on Thursday. "While there is always going to be month-to-month variability, September depletions are trending in the right direction."
The broader backdrop remains challenging for beer sellers. U.S. beer sales fell 1.8% year over year in the two weeks ended September 19, according to Nielsen's latest data.
Still, Fink said September beer depletions improved even beyond the benefit of a later Labor Day, and that the recovery was broad-based across channels. He said consumers were "across the board" engaging in the category.
Some analysts said the results indicated elevated gas prices have dampened Constellation's performance.
“Progress [for Constellation] had accelerated to start 2026, but has been derailed by higher fuel costs,” Roth Capital analyst Bill Kirk wrote, though he said Constellation continues to deliver against its fiscal 2027 plan. Kirk has a buy rating and $209 price target on the stock, compared to the roughly $116 a share price as of Wednesday.
Fink said Constellation saw particular strength in club stores, which have benefited as cash-strapped shoppers seek deals on fuel and groceries. The company is also working to better tailor its product and pack sizes across channels, as consumers make different choices depending on where they are shopping, and for what occasion.
That focus on events also extends to younger drinkers. Fink said consumers are increasingly buying beer for specific moments, rather than treating it as a default purchase, and Constellation is leaning into sports, music, beach activations and other occasions to drive sales.
The company's pricing strategy reflects consumer caution around spending.
CFO Garth Hankinson said Constellation has been selective with price increases, keeping them at the low end of its usual range given the "macroeconomic backdrop and the impact that that's having on our consumer." Hankinson said it is "much more cost-effective to retain your consumers than it is to try to regain your consumers."
That price sensitivity is especially important for Constellation, given its reliance on Hispanic shoppers. About 40% of spending on Constellation's beer comes from Hispanic consumers, compared with roughly 15% for the overall beer category, according to company data.
That cohort has faced more economic concerns , including pressure from the labor market and household finances in part fueled by President Donald Trump's mass deportation policy. Constellation has previously said that beer demand has been weaker in areas with larger Hispanic populations, although it has also pointed to improving trends in some markets.
Constellation is also moving beyond its core beer business. The company announced Tuesday that it would acquire SpikedAde , a spirit-based ready-to-drink beverage brand, for $75 million upfront, with up to another $278 million in potential payments tied to future performance.
The deal gives Constellation a foothold in a new segment that has drawn more interest from consumers. Fink said the company aims to "remain relevant to our consumers and to our customers," adding that distributors have urged Constellation to get into growing categories beyond beer.
Some analysts approved of the move, as well.
"We consider the acquisition attractive, giving [Constellation] exposure to the fast-growing RTD subcategory," said Piper Sandler analyst Michael Lavery, who also noted that Stateside Vodka's competing Super Lyte brand has also had "a very strong start" on the East Coast.
Lavery has a neutral rating and $161 price target on Constellation's stock.
While Fink said beer will remain the company's primary source of value creation, he called SpikedAde a "long, wide-open runway" for Constellation's brand-building and distribution capabilities.
According to the Distilled Spirits Council of the United States, sales of premixed cocktails including spirits-based RTDs grew 16.4% in 2025 to $3.8 billion, making them the spirits industry's strongest growth category.

Defense Minister Boris Pistorius had cancelled a rival F126  frigate project with Dutch company Damen , over delays and cost overruns.
Germany’s far-right AfD party took a significant step toward exercising political power in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
One month after winning 44% of the regional vote, the party secured the presidency of the state parliament, with Tobias Rausch elected as speaker of the house.
What does this moment mean for Germany? DW reports from Magdeburg.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Parliamentarians in Saxony-Anhalt have also voted for AfD politician Hans-Thomas Tillschneider to be one of the deputy speakers in the chamber.
This follows Tobias Rausch of the right-wing populist AfD being voted into the speaker's role earlier on Tuesday.
Tillschneider received 44 votes in favor in Tuesday's session, while 38 parliamentarians opposed his appointment. Nobody abstained from the vote, which was by secret ballot. The AfD has 39 seats in the chamber.
Lawmakers decided to elect three deputy speakers in total, with elections for the others expected to follow later.
Tillschneider, aged 48, is the deputy chair of the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt parliamentary group. He's an AfD veteran, having joined the party in 2013 soon after it was founded.
Tillschneider is a member of the identitarian movement, and was a member of the two AfD fringe groups — the so-called Flügel (wing) and its "Patriotic Platform" — that have since been formally disbanded. He also had close ties to the Pegida and Legida groups that organized anti-migrant protests in eastern Germany.
As well as his strong views on Islam and migration, Tillschneider is also known for his ties to Vladimir Putin's Russia. He was one of three AfD parliamentarians to visit Russia in September 2022, barely six months after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine , in a visit that AfD party co-leader Alice Weidel rapidly disowned as a "private trip" and "not productive."
Since 2023, Tillschneider has written a monthly column for the Vedomosti newspaper in Russia. He attended the 73rd birthday celebrations for Putin at the Russian Embassy in Berlin last October.
The outgoing premier of Saxony-Anhalt says he can't explain where an additional four votes backing the AfD's Tobias Rausch as the state's new parliamentary speaker came from.
In a first for the far-right party, 35-year-old Rausch was elected to the post on Tuesday with the help of the populist BSW party (see entry below).
The Christian Democratic Union (CDU) parliamentary group leadership had recommended that its 15 lawmakers in the state parliament abstain from voting.
But CDU regional leader and current state Premier Sven Schulze said it had become clear by this morning that not all the party's lawmakers planned to do so.
Some indicated that they planned to vote "no," Schulze said in comments to the German press agency DPA. "But none of us said we would vote 'yes,'" he added. "Not a single one."
Rausch was elected with 48 votes in favor and 29 against from 82 eligible votes in the secret ballot. There were five abstentions.
The AfD holds 39 seats in the parliament and the BSW five, meaning Rausch also got backing from members of other parties besides the AfD and BSW.
The center-left Social Democrats demanded answers, with the party's general secretary, Tim Klüssendorf, calling for the CDU to "immediately clarify who from within its ranks may have considered this disastrous decision to be right."
Klüssendorf also criticized the BSW for supporting Rausch's election.
"The BSW has made a conscious decision to elect, for the first time since 1945, a politician from a far-right party to the leadership of a German parliament," Klüssendorf told the Rheinische Post newspaper.
In addition to the CDU, the Social Democrats and the BSW, the Left party and the Greens are also represented in the state's parliament. Except for the BSW, the other parties have refused to work with the AfD, but some combination of them cast a secret vote for Rausch.
The Volksbank Köln Bonn in western Germany has agreed to part ways with a board member, Jürgen Neutgens, after a scandal over a loan he authorized to Cologne 's large brothel, Pascha.
It made the announcement on Tuesday, several months after placing Neutgens on leave and commissioning an independent law firm to investigate the transaction for potential wrongdoing.
"The investigation ... found no indications of financial irregularities or actions contravening obligations in the loan processes or the business relationship," the bank said in a press release . "Nevertheless the past weeks have weighed considerably on everyone involved."
Against this backdrop, the bank said the parties involved had mutually concluded that "a trusting and candid cooperation for the future can no longer be continued on the appropriate foundation."
It said both sides had agreed to confidentiality on the further details and terms, and thanked Neutgens for his service and wished him well for the future.
The loan was issued amid the restrictions of the COVID pandemic, which took a severe toll on the sex industry in Germany and led to the Pascha brothel in Cologne filing for insolvency and then changing ownership .
A family from China, or more specifically the autonomous casino-rich region of Macao, bought the business. But they needed a bridging loan of around €5 million (roughly $5.6 million at today's exchange rates) to cover part of the purchase price when their funds were held up in Hong Kong.
A typical German Christmas speciality intended as a gift for Pope Leo XIV was driven to Rome in an official vehicle from the state of Saxony after it was deemed unsuitable for air transport, officials revealed on Tuesday.
The 4-kilogram (8.8-pound) cake, a so-called stollen, which was made in the Ore Mountains in eastern Germany, was taken by Saxon Premier Michael Kretschmer to the Vatican for a private audience at the end of September.
The cake was reportedly too large to be taken into the cabin and too fragile to be placed in the aircraft hold, the officials said.
No information was provided on the cost by the officials at the Saxon State Chancellery.
The vehicle also transported other presents and documents.
The leader of the Green parliamentary party in Saxony-Anhalt , Susan Sziborra-Seidlitz, has vowed to defend democracy following the election of a member of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) , Tobias Rausch, as parliamentary speaker.
The election of the member of a confirmed right-wing extremist, anti-constitutional party as house speaker meant that a "border" had been crossed, she said.
"We will not allow ourselves to be intimidated, and we will not sit by when rights here or those of the people in this state are to be curtailed," she added.
Earlier in her address, she said that if the AfD were to take power in the state, her party would "speak out if people were denigrated because of their origins, beliefs or lifestyle."
Sziborra-Seidlitz said Saxony-Anhalt could not afford for "exclusion to become the political brand of this parliament and our state."
The AfD emerged from September elections as the strongest single force in parliament but has so far failed to find parties willing to enter into a coalition with it.

Part of a government-funded research project that originated at the University of Warwick, it aims to deploy an autonomous mobility service across the U.K.
Nissan U.K.’s business unit will bring autonomous driving services to the university city of Cambridge and test its latest technology in an urban enviorment and create a blueprint to launch in other communities.
The plans are part of a government-funded research project backed by Nissan that launched in September 2023 at the University of Warwick with the goal of deploying an autonomous mobility service across the U.K.
The pilot trial, dubbed “ADventure,” will be coordinated between the automaker, local authorities, commuters and residents, the company said in its Sept. 28 release .
Using a specially adapted 2022 Nissan Leaf electric vehicle , the project hopes to focus on how future AD technology “can create social value, improve accessibility and address local transport challenges,” Nissan said.
The automaker used the common example of elderly people in the U.K. having to travel to a medical appointment when they do not drive themselves.
Nissan will draw on more than a decade of research by its engineers at the Nissan Technical Center Europe, which will lead the autonomous mobility project.
By choosing the driving environment in Cambridge for the automaker’s first real-world trial, Nissan aims to create a blueprint that it can refine and replicate across the U.K.
“This project is an important step for autonomous mobility in the UK,” said David Moss, SVP research and development for Nissan vehicles across the Africa, Middle East, India, Europe and Oceania regions. “With UK Government backing, it will take autonomous vehicle research beyond central London and into another city, helping us understand how these services can work for different communities and real-life journeys.”
“By developing and applying Nissan’s in-house expertise, combined with the wider knowledge from our partners, we can delve further into how self-driving vehicles can improve connectivity, accessibility and quality of everyday life,” Moss added.

articles.title_orig: World’s largest penguin colony suffers ‘enormous population crash’
articles.title_zh: World’s largest penguin colony suffers ‘enormous population crash’
articles.content_orig:
Chinstrap penguins on Zavodovski Island in Antarctica down by two-thirds since 2011, probably due to climate crisis
The world’s largest penguin colony has declined by two-thirds since 2011, most likely because of the climate crisis, a study has revealed.
Scientists said the rapid demise of chinstrap penguins on Zavodovski, the northernmost of the South Sandwich Islands in Antarctica , increased the risk of a wider ecosystem collapse.
“It is an enormous population crash, equivalent to half a million breeding individuals being lost from that island,” said the leader of the research, Prof Norman Ratcliffe, a penguin ecologist at the British Antarctic Survey .
The Guardian revealed in 2020 that chinstrap penguin populations were decreasing on Low in the South Shetland Islands, prompting concerns among scientists that “something is broken” in the world’s wildest ecosystem.
The new study, published on Wednesday in Current Biology, indicates that the speed of collapse may be accelerating so rapidly that the distinctive bird – which gets its name from a black line that runs below the beak from cheek to cheek – may need to be classified as an endangered species.
The island of Zavodovski had by far the biggest penguin colony in the world, with about 600,000 chinstraps and 90,000 macaroni penguins when the population was measured in 2011. Given the decline between then and 2025, it is likely to have lost that title to Cape Adare in the Ross Sea.
Scientists believe the most likely cause is climate disruption. Human-driven heating has pushed up winter temperatures on and around the Antarctic peninsula to 5C above preindustrial levels, one of the fastest rises in the world. On 6 June, the Argentinian Esperanza base on the Trinity peninsula registered a record winter high of 15.4C, about 20C above normal for the time of year – a margin that scientists described as “absolutely crazy”.
Chinstrap penguins are struggling to adapt because they have special diets and specific ocean temperature preferences. Tracking data shows they prefer to forage in cooler waters to the north-west of the island, where they would expect to find Antarctic krill, which make up the bulk of their diet. But as the waters warm, the krill have moved south into the Weddell Sea.
Macaroni penguins, by contrast, are less fussy eaters and their numbers rose 30% – though not nearly enough to make up for the loss of chinstraps. Ratcliffe said this was only small comfort because if current trends continued, all penguins would run out of space.
after newsletter promotion
He said the loss of chinstrap penguins would have wider repercussions for food webs. “Each ecosystem could be regarded as like a giant Jenga set, and every component that you remove increases the risk of ecosystems collapsing completely.”
The scientists ruled out several other possible causes of decline. There was no sign that chinstrap and macaroni penguins were in competition for food. The nearest humans lived thousands of miles away.
Although the island is volcanic and had a major eruption in 2016, prompting a “Penguin Pompeii hypothesis” of a sudden population fall , this theory was not borne out either by the data, which showed a steady linear decline, or by observations that showed the chinstraps avoided the main “asphyxia plain” area where the ash and lava were deposited.
